about.title: Hanford Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, but proving fault under California law takes more than a bruise and a bad memory. Property owners in Hanford, from grocery stores near 11th Avenue to apartment complexes tucked off 10th Avenue, are only liable if they knew or reasonably should have known about a hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. That's why what you do in the hours and days after a fall matters so much. Photographs of the spilled liquid, the broken step, or the uneven pavement can disappear once the area is cleaned or repaired. Store and apartment surveillance footage is often erased on a short cycle, sometimes within days. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself, but we connect injured Hanford residents with an independent attorney who can move quickly to request that footage, document the scene, and evaluate whether the property owner failed in its duty. There's no charge to get connected, and no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Evidence Matter in a Hanford Fall Claim

items.title: Proving the Owner Had Notice
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can dig into maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to build that case.

items.title: Racing the Surveillance Clock
items.desc: Many Hanford businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having video evidence and having none.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery can be reduced but not eliminated if you're found partly responsible. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that fairly reflects what actually happened.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Hanford?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is government-owned, such as a Kings County building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim, so it's wise to act promptly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my fall?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so being partially responsible doesn't automatically bar your claim. Your potential recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, which an attorney can help evaluate.

items.question: I fell in a parking lot near N 11th Avenue in Hanford, does that change anything?
items.answer: Not necessarily, but the specific location matters for identifying who owns or maintains the property, whether a private business, a landlord, or a public entity. That ownership question affects both the deadline and how the claim is handled, which is something an independent attorney can sort out quickly.
